clue.text: Savage to be issued with a rule when moving around prison

parts.note: an order or decree that is issued is said to go forth

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit on either side of the prison word
the letters are set in motion, so they rearrange

parts.note: jug is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A prisoner is handed a rule while being moved round the jail and turns violent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when moving' shuffles the two words into EULAR, which 'around' splits so the prison word sits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To go for the jugular is to attack viciously at the most vulnerable point, so a savage verbal onslaught.

clue.text: Attractive lace with marvellous wrapping

indicators.note: the marvellous word is wrapped round the lace word

parts.note: magic used as an adjective means marvellous
net is a lace-like fabric

explanation.surface: Pretty lace looks wonderful when used to wrap something.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic means drawing things towards it, literally or in charm and personality.

clue.text: Conflict in social worker's mind

indicators.note: the conflict word goes inside the worker word

parts.note: a bee is a social insect and a worker bee is the classic crossword worker
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A social worker is troubled by inner conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'social worker' is not a caseworker but an insect that lives in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Mind as an imperative warning, as in mind the gap, is a synonym of beware.

clue.text: One's up for living here

parts.note: being up means being in residence at university, and a student lives in this college building

explanation.surface: Someone keen on being alive is described as wanting to live in a place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' is the British university sense: a student who is up is in residence for term.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall of residence is student accommodation where those up at university live.

clue.text: Satellites set in pods sent up

indicators.note: the set word goes inside the pods word
in a down clue, sent up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: pods are the skins of peas and beans
to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: Satellites are placed in capsules and launched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns the pods word into SNIKS before the set word goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputnik was the name of the first Soviet artificial satellites, launched from 1957.

clue.text: Half of wrong jabs uncovered — targeted group may get this

indicators.note: only the first half of the wrong word is kept

parts.note: an injury is a wrong done to someone, in the legal sense

indicators.note: the outer letters are stripped off like a cover

parts.note: jabs and pokes are both prods

explanation.surface: Wrong injections given openly to a target group of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes INJ from INJURY; 'uncovered' strips POKES to OKE.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-joke is humour shared and understood only by a particular circle of people.

clue.text: Policeman and clergyman stand above common CEO

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit above the last one

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
a rector is a parish priest
general means common, as in general opinion

explanation.surface: A police officer and a priest rank higher than an ordinary chief executive.
explanation.definitionFit: A director-general is the head of an organisation such as the BBC, the equivalent of a chief executive.

clue.text: Put a little nosegay over back passage

indicators.note: the run of letters is read backwards
only a little of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Someone is told to tuck a small posy over their back passage, comically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put a little' takes EGAYOV from inside 'nosegay over' and 'back' turns it round. 'back passage' looks like one phrase; only 'passage' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a journey by sea, which is what a voyage is.

clue.text: Associated Press write papers about Times supplement

parts.note: AP is the standard abbreviation for the news agency
to pen is to write

indicators.note: the papers word turns about, reading backwards

parts.note: ID means identity papers
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A news agency writes papers on a supplement to The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ID into DI. 'Times' is not the newspaper but the times sign.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendix is supplementary material added at the end of a book.

clue.text: County Hall's opening cancelled on order of Crown

indicators.note: in an across clue the hall piece comes on, that is after, the reordered word
the letters of the word are put in a new order
the first letter is cancelled

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive dropped

explanation.surface: The opening of the County Hall is called off by royal command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'County Hall' looks like the definition-plus-building; only 'County' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornwall is the county at the south-western tip of England.

clue.text: Open drier with right tool

indicators.note: the drier word is opened up and the right letter put inside

parts.note: a towel is used to dry with

explanation.surface: Someone opens a tumble dryer while holding the right tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' splits TOWEL to take R: T-R-OWEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand tool for gardening or spreading mortar.

clue.text: National icon trusty, albeit worried about backing adversary

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the reversed enemy
the letters are worried, that is agitated, into a new order
the adversary word is read backwards

parts.note: a foe is an adversary

explanation.surface: A dependable national symbol is nevertheless anxious about supporting an enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' shuffles TRUSTY ALBEIT into STATU-LIBERTY, 'backing' turns FOE to EOF, and 'about' puts it in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Statue of Liberty in New York harbour is an emblem of the United States.

clue.text: Station requires select ground to provide coverage for area

indicators.note: the shuffled letters cover, that is surround, the area letter
ground means crushed, so the letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: A station needs carefully selected land to give cover for its surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requires' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester Square is a London Underground station in the West End.

clue.text: Apprehension to prosecute former poet after repeated cuts

indicators.note: repeated says the cut made to the poet is made to the prosecute word too

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action against someone

indicators.note: cuts means the poet's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Edmund Spenser was an Elizabethan poet

explanation.surface: A prosecutor feels anxious about a dead poet after cuts are made again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated cuts' trims the last letter from both words, SU(E) and SPENSE(R).
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is anxious uncertainty while waiting for something to happen.

clue.text: Rain gauge outside old cathedral is computerised centrally

indicators.note: the central letters are placed outside the cathedral word
only the central letters of the word are taken

parts.note: dome is an archaic word for a cathedral, as in Italian duomo

explanation.surface: A rain gauge outside an ancient cathedral is run by a central computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centrally' takes the middle four letters of the twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: A udometer is a technical name for an instrument measuring rainfall, from Latin udus, wet.

clue.text: Fights following proposal to make containers for kites?

indicators.note: the fights word comes after the proposal word

parts.note: a suggestion is a proposal
boxes means fights with fists

explanation.surface: Boxing bouts come after a proposal to build containers for toy kites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kites' are ideas, as in flying a kite to test opinion, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A suggestion box collects ideas put forward, and flying a kite means floating a tentative idea.

clue.text: Almost look upon arbitrator to break agreement?

indicators.note: in a down clue the look piece sits upon the arbitrator piece
the look word stops one letter short

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily
ump is short for umpire, an arbitrator

explanation.surface: Someone tries to look at an umpire nearly enough to wreck a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: GAZUMP is a British term: a seller accepts a higher offer after agreeing a price with another buyer.
explanation.definitionFit: To gazump is to go back on an agreed house sale by accepting a higher bid.

clue.text: Sons keeping clear of unnecessary rivalry

indicators.note: the sons letters are kept out of the word

parts.note: needless means unnecessary
S is the abbreviation for son, so two sons give two of them

explanation.surface: Sons avoiding pointless competition between them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping clear of' removes SS from NEEDLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Needle is hostility between competitors, as in a needle match between old rivals.

clue.text: German quietly avoiding problem wolf

indicators.note: the quiet letter is avoided, so left out

parts.note: a puzzle is a problem
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A German quietly sidesteps the problem of a wolf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wolf' is a verb, to eat greedily, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To wolf food and to guzzle it both mean eating or drinking greedily.

clue.text: Regard flat just over the bridge

parts.note: to eye is to regard
level means flat

explanation.surface: Someone looks at an apartment just across the bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' is not an apartment but an adjective, and 'the bridge' is the bridge of the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The eyes sit just above the bridge of the nose, so that height is eye level.

clue.text: What might notedly bring up racism?

definitions.text: What might notedly bring up racism?

indicators.note: the clue's question asks what the letters of the two words might be brought round to form

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of music might raise racism as a topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring' rearranges UP RACISM, and the whole clue describes the answer: 'notedly' means in musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rap music often tackles social issues, and lyrics about racism are a recurring theme of the genre.

clue.text: Latitude of unknown Scottish well towards the west

indicators.note: in an across clue, westward means right to left, so the Scottish word reads backwards

parts.note: aweel is a Scots interjection meaning well
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: The latitude of a Scottish well whose location is unknown, lying westwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'towards the west' reverses AWEEL to LEEWA, ahead of Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway and latitude both mean freedom or room to manoeuvre.
